title: Alexander Chernetsky, the Kharkiv-born singer-songwriter who led the rock band Raznye Lyudi, dies at 60
text: Alexander Chernetsky, a singer-songwriter, composer, and frontman of the rock band Raznye Lyudi, has died at 60, musician Garik Sukachev said. “Some sad news. Alexander Chernetsky, a wonderful musician and the leader of Raznye Lyudi, has passed away. Rest in peace,” Sukachev wrote on social media. Alexander Chernetsky A source close to Chernetsky told TASS that he died on November 8 after a long illness. Chernetsky was born on January 10, 1966, in Kharkiv. He began performing in 1983, when he formed a school band called Karbonarii with his cousin. He later formed Rock Front, which was renamed Raznye Lyudi. The band initially performed in Kharkiv, but after moving to St. Petersburg, Chernetsky assembled a new lineup of Raznye Lyudi. Chernetsky was diagnosed with ankylosing spondylitis, a condition that causes chronic inflammation of the joints and spine. The illness forced him to take breaks from performing. Raznye Lyudi has released about 20 albums, some recorded with Sergei Chigrakov and his band Chizh & Co. Chernetsky also released two solo albums. title: Zelensky says Russia is ‘trying to divide Ukraine along the Dnipro River’ with strikes on bridges and the power grid
text: Russian forces are “trying to divide Ukraine along the Dnipro River” by striking bridges and the power grid, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in an evening televised address. He also said Russia’s strikes aimed to “make life as difficult as possible for people, for our cities and villages.” The Financial Times reported that Zelensky also told European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen that Russia was trying to destroy bridges across the Dnipro to divide Ukraine. A Ukrainian official told the newspaper that information available to Kyiv indicated Russia planned to disrupt transportation and shipments of equipment and ammunition across the Dnipro and reduce the flow of electricity from the country’s west to its east. In winter, he said, this would leave millions of people across the country without electricity or heat. In October, Russian forces began heavily striking bridges across the Dnipro in Kyiv. The strikes have forced bridge closures, causing hours-long traffic jams.
